findings.summary: Acceptance step 2 is only half evidenced. harness/state/evidence/gates/3.R2/ holds only the full gate run, which passed: ok, clean_tree true, at c7561f2, 10 commands exit 0. It holds no gate pg evidence. The implementer's manual Postgres run (119 passed) is a claim in the report, not gate evidence. The controller must run gate pg on a clean tree before it sets passes for F-3-R2. close-check already refuses to close for this reason (feature does not pass, no handoff, no progress entry).

FA-2 has two halves, and only the repeat half has a test (test_repeat_fallback_hands_on_the_moved_run, which spies on _rationale_probe and checks that the revision matches the store). The typed-answer grounding half, run = probe.run or run, has no test. The code is correct by reading: _fell_back returns what record_fallback returns (features.py:363-374). The report says no observable consumer follows that line today. FA-2 was originally Low/style.
The handoff's What changed row for 3.R2 reads '`5a1d960`, then the docs commit'. There are two docs commits, e9b8fe0 and c7561f2, and the row names neither. The 3.R1 row names all of its hashes.

The P-5 row changes the recorded wording of the finding: 'with no gate enforcing the limit' was dropped from the Finding column. The correction belongs only in the Handled column. The correction itself is right: tests/unit/kernel/test_structure.py:72 enforces MAX_KERNEL_MODULE_LINES = 500.

An unbound run's admission checks only the agent-visible capabilities (the brief's definition). _handle_proposal has no agent_visible check, so in principle a model could propose a host-only write in an unbound run that has been admitted. Today every host-only capability is a read (erp domain manifest :101, :228, :323), so this is latent. Checking every registered capability for a run that is not bound would close the gap at no cost, because host-only reads are READ.
